questions.question_text: Wafer capsule is known as
questions.explanation: Cachets are also known as wafer capsules, historically used to enclose disagreeable powders.

questions.question_text: The pigment in the rod cells of eye is called as
questions.explanation: Rhodopsin is the biological pigment found in the rods of the retina that is sensitive to light.

questions.question_text: Vitamin K deficiency results in the disorder
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the hepatic synthesis of blood clotting factors, and its deficiency leads to bleeding disorders.

questions.question_text: A diuretic drug
questions.explanation: Gokhru (Tribulus terrestris) is traditionally known and used for its diuretic properties.

questions.question_text: Baljet test is used for
questions.explanation: Baljet test is a chemical test specifically used for the detection of cardiac glycosides (specifically active methylene groups).

questions.question_text: In modern medicine Cocaine is used as
questions.explanation: Cocaine is occasionally used medically as a topical local anesthetic for mucous membranes in ENT procedures.

questions.question_text: Choose a plant which contain Cardiac glycosides.
questions.explanation: Digitalis species contain potent cardiac glycosides such as digoxin and digitoxin.

questions.question_text: Papaverine shows which pharmacological activity ?
questions.explanation: Papaverine is an opium alkaloid used primarily for the treatment of visceral spasm and vasospasm.

questions.question_text: Jesuit's bark is synonym of
questions.explanation: Cinchona bark is historically known as Jesuit's bark due to its introduction to Europe by Jesuit missionaries.

questions.question_text: In paracetamol poisoning N acetyl cysteine act as a
questions.explanation: N-acetylcysteine acts as a glutathione precursor and substitute to detoxify the toxic NAPQI metabolite in paracetamol overdose.

questions.question_text: A selective beta blocker
questions.explanation: Atenolol is a cardioselective ($beta_1$) blocking agent, whereas propranolol, timolol, and nadolol are non-selective.

questions.question_text: Madrell's salt is used as
questions.explanation: Madrell's salt (insoluble sodium metaphosphate) is commonly used as a polishing agent in dentifrices.

questions.question_text: A respiratory stimulant
questions.explanation: Ammonium carbonate acts as a reflex respiratory stimulant (smelling salt) by irritating the mucous membranes of the nose.

questions.question_text: Haloperidol is classified as a
questions.explanation: Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic drug belonging to the butyrophenone chemical class.

questions.question_text: Which of the following metal has no therapeutic use ?
questions.explanation: Lead is a toxic heavy metal with no approved therapeutic use in modern medicine.

questions.question_text: Who proposed the double helical model of DNA ?
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double helix structure of DNA in 1953.

questions.question_text: An unsaturated fatty acid
questions.explanation: Oleic acid contains a double bond, making it an unsaturated fatty acid, unlike stearic, palmitic, and myristic acids which are saturated.

questions.question_text: A mucopolysaccharide
questions.explanation: Heparin is a sulfated glycosaminoglycan, historically classified as a mucopolysaccharide.

questions.question_text: The Vitamin isolated from egg yolk
questions.explanation: Biotin (Vitamin H / B7) was originally isolated in large quantities from egg yolk.

questions.question_text: Multiple forms of the same enzyme are called
questions.explanation: Isoenzymes (or isozymes) are enzymes that differ in amino acid sequence but catalyze the same chemical reaction.

questions.question_text: RNA synthesis on DNA strand is known as
questions.explanation: Transcription is the process of synthesizing an RNA molecule from a DNA template strand.

questions.question_text: The drug which produces reddish brown coloration of the skin after administration
questions.explanation: Clofazimine is known to cause a characteristic reddish-brown to black skin discoloration in patients undergoing treatment.

questions.question_text: The Schedule which describes the guidelines on clinical trials
questions.explanation: Schedule Y under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act outlines the requirements and guidelines for clinical trials in India.

questions.question_text: The Poison Act was passed in the year
questions.explanation: The Poison Act in India was enacted in the year 1919 (Act No. 12 of 1919, passed on 3rd September 1919 - though option A/D ranges, 1919 is standard).

questions.question_text: Schedule V describes

options.B: Standards for patent or proprietary medicines

questions.explanation: Schedule V of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules prescribes standards for patent or proprietary medicines / cosmetics depending on specific jurisdictions, but Schedule S is cosmetics; let's verify: Schedule S is cosmetics, Schedule M is GMP, Schedule O is disinfectant. Schedule V covers standards for patent/proprietary medicines or standard reference.

questions.question_text: Which of the following contains sulphur in its elemental composition ?
questions.explanation: Benzylpenicillin contains a thiazolidine ring which incorporates a sulfur atom in its chemical structure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is used to treat nausea and vomiting associated with cancer chemotherapy ?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron is a selective $5-HT_3$ receptor antagonist widely used to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

questions.question_text: How many ex-officio members are there in Pharmacy Council of India ?
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy Council of India includes 3 ex-officio members (Director General of Health Services, Director of the Central Drugs Laboratory, and Drugs Controller General of India).

questions.question_text: Drugs Inspectors are appointed under which Section of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act ?
questions.explanation: Section 21 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act empowers the central or state government to appoint Drug Inspectors.

questions.question_text: An aryl propionic acid derivative
questions.explanation: Ibuprofen is a well-known nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug belonging to the arylpropionic acid class.

questions.question_text: The MTP Act was passed in the year
questions.explanation: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in 1971.

questions.question_text: If a drug is imported under a name which belongs to another drug, such drugs are known as (as per D and C Act and Rules)
questions.explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, a drug is considered 'misbranded' if it is imported under the name of another drug.

questions.question_text: What is Form-12 as per Drugs and Cosmetics Act?

options.A: Application for licence to import drugs specified in Sch. X
options.B: Application for licence to import drugs for the purpose of examination, test or analysis
options.C: Application for licence to import small quantities of drugs by a Govt. hospital
options.D: Form of undertaking to accompany an application for an import licence

questions.explanation: Form 12 under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act is used for applying for a license to import drugs for the purpose of examination, test, or analysis.

questions.question_text: A second generation H1 antagonist
questions.explanation: Astemisole is a non-sedating, second-generation H1 receptor antagonist.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an anorectic agent?
questions.explanation: Fenfluramine is a well-known centrally acting anorectic agent used as an appetite suppressant.

questions.question_text: Indirectly acting sympathomimetic drug
questions.explanation: Amphetamine (spelled Amphitamine in the text) is an indirectly acting sympathomimetic drug that releases stored catecholamines.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs does not contain Indole alkaloid?
questions.explanation: Ephedra contains ephedrine, which is a proto-alkaloid (phenylalkylamine derivative), not an indole alkaloid.

questions.question_text: Phytolaca Americana is the adulterant of
questions.explanation: Pokeweed (Phytolaca americana) roots and leaves are known adulterants for Belladonna root and leaves.

questions.question_text: The enzyme diastase belongs to the family
questions.explanation: Diastase is typically obtained from malt (derived from barley, Gramineae) or fungi such as Saccharomyces species (Saccharomycetaceae).

questions.question_text: Million reagent is used to identify
questions.explanation: Millon's reagent is used for the detection of proteins and amino acids containing phenol groups, such as gelatin and tyrosine-containing proteins.

questions.question_text: Baudoin's test is used to identify
questions.explanation: Baudouin test is a specific chemical test used to detect the presence of sesame oil.

questions.question_text: Pyrethrum belongs to the family
questions.explanation: Pyrethrum belongs to the family Compositae (Asteraceae).

questions.question_text: Clavenger apparatus is used for the estimation of
questions.explanation: Clevenger apparatus is standard laboratory equipment used to extract and estimate volatile oils by steam distillation.

questions.question_text: The drug which is not obtained from seeds
questions.explanation: Asafoetida is an oleo-gum-resin obtained from the rhizome and roots of Ferula species, not from seeds.

questions.question_text: Hager's reagent is a solution of
questions.explanation: Hager's reagent is a saturated aqueous solution of picric acid used for the detection of alkaloids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a cyanogenetic glycoside?
questions.explanation: Amygdalin is a well-known cyanogenic glycoside found in bitter almonds and kernels of Prunus species.

questions.question_text: Immuno modulating drug
questions.explanation: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is widely recognized in Ayurveda and modern studies for its immunomodulatory properties.

questions.question_text: Gray baby syndrome is produced by
questions.explanation: Gray baby syndrome is a serious adverse effect associated with high systemic levels of the antibiotic chloramphenicol in newborns.

questions.question_text: A benzomorphan derivative
questions.explanation: Pentazocine belongs to the benzomorphan class of opioid analgesics.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is racemic compound?
questions.explanation: Atropine is the racemic mixture (dl-hyoscyamine) of the naturally occurring levorotatory hyoscyamine.

questions.question_text: Glycogenolysis is the breakdown of stored glycogen to
questions.explanation: Glycogenolysis is the biochemical pathway through which glycogen molecules are broken down into glucose-1-phosphate and subsequently glucose.

questions.question_text: Which one is a ketone body?
questions.explanation: Beta-hydroxybutyrate, along with acetoacetate and acetone, is classified as one of the primary ketone bodies produced by the liver.

questions.question_text: A ketogenic amino acid
questions.explanation: Leucine is purely ketogenic, while lysine is both ketogenic and glucogenic.

questions.question_text: Average life span of erythrocytes in humans
questions.explanation: The average lifespan of circulating human red blood cells (erythrocytes) is approximately 120 days.

questions.question_text: Milky white color of urine is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: Chyluria, the presence of fat globules (lymph/chyle) in the urine, causes it to appear milky white.

questions.question_text: Severe form of anaemia
questions.explanation: Hemolytic anemia can manifest as a severe form of anemia due to the rapid destruction of red blood cells.

questions.question_text: Molisch's reagent is used to detect the presence of
questions.explanation: Molisch's test is a sensitive chemical test for the presence of carbohydrates, such as lactose.

questions.question_text: Unequal distribution of color on the surface of colored tablets is called as
questions.explanation: Mottling is a tablet defect characterized by an unequal distribution of color on the tablet surface.

questions.question_text: The material used in enteric coating
questions.explanation: Cellulose acetate phthalate (CAP) is a classic pH-sensitive polymer widely used for enteric coating.

questions.question_text: Alkylation of proteins molecules is the mechanism of sterilization by
questions.explanation: Ethylene oxide acts as a sterilizing agent by alkylating functional groups of proteins and nucleic acids.

questions.question_text: 1 fluid ounce
questions.explanation: One fluid ounce in the US/Imperial system is approximately equal to $29.57\text{ ml}$, commonly rounded to $30\text{ ml}$ in pharmacy calculations.

questions.question_text: The first edition of Pharmacopoeia of India was published in
questions.explanation: The first official edition of the Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP) was published in 1955.

questions.question_text: The mill which works on the principle of impact and attrition
questions.explanation: A hammer mill operates primarily on the principle of impact between rapidly moving hammers and particles, along with attrition.

questions.question_text: The ratio $4:2:1$ ($	ext{oil} : 	ext{water} : 	ext{gum}$) can be used for which oil?
questions.explanation: Fixed oils like almond oil typically require a primary emulsion ratio of $4:2:1$ (oil:water:gum) using the Continental method.

questions.question_text: Oleoginous ointment base contain
questions.explanation: Liquid paraffin is a fundamental hydrocarbon component of oleaginous (hydrocarbon) ointment bases.

questions.question_text: Which is a Prodrug?
questions.explanation: Levodopa is a metabolic precursor (prodrug) of dopamine that crosses the blood-brain barrier.

questions.question_text: Which drug induces Parkinsonism?
questions.explanation: Chlorpromazine, a typical antipsychotic, blocks dopamine D2 receptors and frequently induces extrapyramidal side effects resembling Parkinsonism.

questions.question_text: HMG CoA reductase inhibitor drug
questions.explanation: Atorvastatin belongs to the statin class, which competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase.

questions.question_text: A potassium sparing diuretic
questions.explanation: Triamterene (spelled Triam terene in OCR) is a direct-acting potassium-sparing diuretic.

questions.question_text: Drug which produces ototoxicity
questions.explanation: Aminoglycoside antibiotics like streptomycin are well known to cause dose-dependent ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.

questions.question_text: Steven Johnson syndrome is exhibited by
questions.explanation: Sulfonamides, such as sulfadimidine, are frequently associated with severe cutaneous adverse reactions like Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a quinolone derivative?
questions.explanation: Nalidixic acid is the first-generation prototype synthetic quinolone antibacterial agent.

questions.question_text: Opium alkaloid containing isoquinoline ring system is
questions.explanation: Papaverine belongs to the benzylisoquinoline structural class of opium alkaloids, unlike morphine and codeine which are phenanthrene derivatives.

questions.question_text: A drug which holds a phenoxy acetic acid ring system
questions.explanation: Ethacrynic acid is a loop diuretic containing a phenoxyacetic acid chemical nucleus.

questions.question_text: The diagnostic agent which is used for kidney function test
questions.explanation: Indigo carmine (indigocarmine) is a dye historically used in chromocystoscopy to evaluate renal function and ureteral patency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following oils is used as a vehicle for oily injectables?
questions.explanation: Arachis oil (peanut oil) is frequently purified and used as a non-aqueous vehicle for intramuscular oil-based injections.

questions.question_text: Solanaceous alkaloids are present in
questions.explanation: Datura belongs to the Solanaceae family and contains tropane alkaloids like hyoscyamine and scopolamine.

questions.question_text: Sometime large dose of a drug is required to elicit a response usually obtained by normal therapeutic dose. Such a phenomenon is termed as
questions.explanation: Drug tolerance refers to a decreased responsiveness to a drug's pharmacological effects following repeated administration, requiring higher doses.

questions.question_text: The injection given in between the first and second cervical vertebrae is called
questions.explanation: Injection into the cisterna magna between the atlas (first cervical vertebra) and axis (second cervical vertebra) is known as an intracisternal injection.

questions.question_text: Tetracycline is found in large quantities in
questions.explanation: Tetracyclines readily chelate calcium ions and deposit in calcified tissues such as bones and teeth in high concentrations.

questions.question_text: Which one of the soil found in India is the most useful for agriculture?
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil is considered the most fertile and agriculturally useful soil in India.

questions.question_text: The least populated Union Territory is
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep has the lowest population among all the Union Territories of India.

questions.question_text: In India which coast receives rainfall from North East Monsoon?
questions.explanation: The Coromandel coast receives the majority of its rainfall from the Northeast Monsoon during the winter months.

questions.question_text: In which year Hindustan Socialist Republican Association is formed?
questions.explanation: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi.

questions.question_text: Who among the following is known as the heroine of 1942 Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: Aruna Asaf Ali is widely remembered as the heroine of the 1942 Quit India Movement for hoisting the Indian National flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan.

questions.question_text: NITI Aayog
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog is neither a statutory body nor simply a consultative body in the traditional sense; it is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory policy think tank of the Government of India.

questions.question_text: Mudra Yojana is intended to

options.B: Resolve to provide a home to each poor family
options.C: Empower rural women by helping them form self help groups
options.D: Loan for small entrepreneurs without any guarantor or mortgage

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana provides loans up to 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises without requiring collateral.

questions.question_text: The thermal power plant of National Thermal Power Corporation is being constructed in ________ district.
questions.explanation: The NTPC thermal power project in Kerala is located at Cheemeni in Kasaragod, or closely associated with projects like the Rajiv Gandhi Combined Cycle Power Plant in Kayamkulam (Alappuzha); however, specific context points to the Cheemeni/Kannur region or specific regional exams.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the largest lake in Kerala?
questions.explanation: Vembanad Lake is the longest lake in India and the largest lake in the state of Kerala.

questions.question_text: Kerala stands first in the production of ________ among Indian States.
questions.explanation: Kerala is the largest producer of natural rubber in India.

questions.question_text: Prathyaksha Raksha Daiva Sabha was founded by
questions.explanation: Prathyaksha Raksha Daiva Sabha (PRDS) was founded by Poykayil Yohannan, also known as Kumara Gurudevan, in 1909.

questions.question_text: "Sivayogavilasam" the monthly was published by
questions.explanation: Vagbhatananda founded the Atma Vidya Sangham and published the magazine Sivayogavilasam.

questions.question_text: Ayya Vazhi is the dharmic belief system centered on the life and preaching of
questions.explanation: Ayyavazhi is an henotheistic belief system centered on the life and teachings of Ayya Vaikundar.

questions.question_text: Ananda Mahasabha was founded by
questions.explanation: Ananda Mahasabha was founded by Swami Brahmananda Sivayogi.

questions.question_text: Who raised the slogan No Caste, No Religion, No God for human being?
questions.explanation: Sahodaran Ayyappan famously coined and raised the slogan 'No caste, no religion, no God for man'.

questions.question_text: The Bengali literature who received the Jnanapith Award in 2016
questions.explanation: Bengali poet Sankha Ghosh (often transcribed as Sangha Gosh) received the Jnanapith Award for 2016.

questions.question_text: Which Indian badminton player won the Women's single title in the 2017 Malaysia Masters prix?
questions.explanation: Saina Nehwal won the Women's singles title at the Malaysia Masters Grand Prix Gold in 2017.

questions.question_text: 'The Art of the Deal' is the autobiography of
questions.explanation: 'Trump: The Art of the Deal' is a 1987 book credited to Donald J. Trump and journalist Tony Schwartz.

questions.question_text: Who is the newly appointed Director of CBI?
questions.explanation: Alok Verma was appointed as the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in early 2017.

questions.question_text: Meenakshi Amma winner of Padmashri Award 2017, famous in field of
questions.explanation: Meenakshi Amma received the Padma Shri in 2017 for her expertise and contribution to Kalaripayattu, the traditional martial art of Kerala.
